Root cause measured: updatePivot wrote the pointer position straight into the constraint, so the hand teleported up to 234px per frame (p90 107) and whipped the rat to 249px/step against 44px bumpers - Matter has no continuous collision detection, so more than half of all steps moved further than a bumper is wide. Measuring rope segment velocity directly (with sub-stepping, body.velocity IS per-sub-step displacement) shows why my hand=40 recommendation was wrong: I estimated rope displacement from the RAT peak, but rope segments whip far faster than the rat (432 vs 247 px/step). SCOPE SET 2026-09-12: user chose a full design gate over a quick constant change. THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM the design must solve: the goal is to destroy YOUR OWN rat in as few hits as possible and score is max(200, 3000-(hits-1)*500), so taking more damage per hit is purely good - there is no downside to trade against, and any variant with a higher multiplier is permanently strictly better. The usual counterweight is unavailable too: heavy mass 11.5 should swing slower, but the player drives the pivot directly so the hand overrides mass, which is why both variants clock identical in-play speed (114.1 vs 114.4). Mass-based trade-offs do not survive this control scheme. Options sketched and NOT chosen: cut heavy impactMultiplier 2.2 -> ~1.25; equalise damage and differentiate on feel/blast/appearance; keep heavy strong but apply a score penalty. Also note the arithmetic trap: standard needs ~3.3x damage to reach 4 hits on L1, which would drop heavy to ~1.4 hits, so DAMAGE_SCALE cannot move until this resolves. NOT solved, and INVERTED: standard now out-scores heavy by 800 on average (3800 vs 3000), so standard is the dominant pick. Both variants now play in a 2-4 hit band with means 3.4 and 3.0, which is indistinguishable at n=5, and the precision axis (31% vs 15% glancing) that the whole design rested on does not translate into a hit-count difference at this damage scale. A 3-4 hit target simply leaves no room to express variant difference - there is nowhere in a 2-4 band to put a gap. REOPENED WIDER 2026-09-13: task 143 refuted the precision premise outright (heavy glances MORE, 28.6% vs 19.3%), so the difficulty-selector answer to 126 has no support. Heavy remains stronger by exactly its 1.4x multiplier with nothing offsetting it - the ORIGINAL 126 problem, in smaller form. 126 cannot close until task 144 re-pitches damage, because hit counts will move and the variant comparison has to be re-read on the new numbers. task: The rat can escape the arena - no ceiling, and no CCD against 50px walls

context: Reported by the user 2026-09-16 - the rat occasionally gets caught off screen or beyond the boundary. Two independent causes, both structural. (2) The rat has no continuous collision detection - sweeping was applied to rope segments only, deliberately, on the grounds that the rat is large and carries the damage - but the walls are 50px thick and CLAUDE.md itself records ~50 px/step as the single-step tunneling threshold for a 50px wall, while measured rat peak speed runs 250-460 px/step. Once outside, the rat would have to tunnel back to return, which matches 'caught'. Cheapest likely fix is much thicker walls plus a ceiling, which costs nothing per step and changes no game feel; extending the rope's sweep to the rat is the alternative but would touch the body that carries the damage. DONE 2026-09-16 on branch swinging/fix/arena-containment: a ceiling added and every boundary thickened to 800px, against measured rat peaks of 250-460 px/step. THE GUARD IS STRUCTURAL, NOT BEHAVIOURAL, and that was earned: the first version whipped the hand at the boundaries and PASSED with the ceiling deliberately removed, because the escape took 90 iterations to reproduce and the check ran 80. SCOPE EXPANDED 2026-09-14 by the user, who asked for three things to be folded in here rather than filed separately - they are level-design vocabulary, which is what this gate exists to decide. NOTE THE PRECEDENT: a hand constraint was tried before - the `hand` dev knob capping px per frame - and the 2026-09-11 decision records it as having capped the skill ceiling while not fixing the tunneling it was for. A positional zone is a different constraint (where, not how fast) and plausibly increases skill expression rather than capping it, but the design should engage with that history rather than rediscover it. Also connects to the task 149 finding that shield placement dominated shield tier: if where the player can be is the strongest lever, a zone controls it directly instead of regulating it downstream. (2) BLADE/RAZOR OBSTACLE: cuts the tail and fails the level. Feasible specifically because of the task 124 link-level CCD work, which took rope link crossings from 5-7.5% to under 1% - without accurate rope collision a blade would kill through phantom contacts the renderer never drew. task: Angle-rewarding target shapes - eight shapes, one per cardinal and diagonal
context: User idea 2026-09-20: a target shape that grants more damage when struck from a particular direction (e.g. from below), so a level can be built around approaching from that side. Needs a design pass - it touches the damage formula, which has exactly one direction term today (angleFactor, the dot product of approach and surface normal) and no notion of a preferred side. Run /brainstorm. Designed 2026-09-20 and split into 184-186; see that day's decision entry.

task: The rat tunnels through shield panels - it has no continuous collision and panels are 12-14px thick
context: Measured 2026-09-20, answering the user question "sometimes I hit the target before breaking any shield": four hits landed on caged targets while the cage still stood, at 48, 52, 60 and 61 px/step through a 14px panel. Only the ROPE is swept (physics.js sweepRopeSegments / resolveRopeLinks); the rat deliberately has none, which is why the arena walls are 800px thick. A shield is the thinnest solid body in the game, so it is the one that leaks. Thickening panels cannot fix it (rat peaks 250-460 px/step); the fix is to sweep the rat against shield bodies, reusing the rope machinery. FIXED 2026-09-20 with Physics.sweepRat (rewind-only, velocity untouched). A/B over 3 reps of a 16-run sequence: 3 tunnelled hits every rep without it, 0 with it. Bot clears on the cage levels fall 16/16 -> 14-15/16 because the bot arrives at ~46 px/step against light 45 and must now break a panel it used to slip through; humans broke that cage 4/4, so nothing was retuned. dev/smoke.mjs also had a hardcoded 9-level count - now asserts only that levels render, since the gate owns the exact number.

task: L11 First Cut - move the blade to the diagonal the user drew, and ease cutSpeed
context: Playtest feedback 2026-09-20 with a sketch (temp/level 11 feedback.png): the blade moves from horizontal overhead to a diagonal running up-to-the-right between the hand and the target, roughly (577,325)-(755,168) in canvas px, so ~x 0.605 y 0.397, length ~237, angle ~-41 deg. It also cut 2 of 7 runs at 230 (tail speeds 233 and 272) against the <= 20% rule-7 criterion, so ease the threshold as well - but the diagonal changes which speeds ever reach it, so re-measure rather than trusting a number picked now. DONE 2026-09-20: blade moved to the sketched diagonal (x 0.605, y 0.398, w 237, angle -41) and cutSpeed 230 -> 280. Screenshot matches the sketch; bot 8/8 cleared, 0 cut - which says nothing about the human cut rate (at a shared 120 the bot gave 0/8 against a human 45%). The threshold is a starting point, not a measurement: a blade in the swing path is crossed far more often than an overhead one, so it needs the next playtest.
